summary: Tested the store-picker fix (1..7 stores) and the watchlist card redesign (photo thumbnail, trash icon below the 'Usually' price). Backend: 14/15 new iteration-6 tests pass. PUT /api/me/onboarding saves all 7 stores and single stores (Aldi, H-E-B, Tom Thumb), returns 422 for 0 or 8 stores and 400 for unknown stores, and deals from removed stores are dropped. GET /api/watchlist returns image_url and image_checked. The background lookup marks every item as checked, POST sets image_checked=false, PUT resets the image, and delete/restore keeps image_url. One failure: duplicate stores are saved as-is. Regression: 110 of 112 pass. I updated 2 old tests that assumed 2-4 stores. test_check_live gave one 502 in the parallel run and passed on rerun (flaky). Frontend at 390x844 in demo mode: Profile > Stores & ZIP shows 3/7, then tapping Aldi, H-E-B, Tom Thumb and Sprouts all check (count 4/7 to 7/7). Save stores returns to Profile, which shows all 7 chips. Deselecting all gives 0/7 with Save disabled; 1 store (Tom Thumb) saves, and Deals shows only the Tom Thumb chip. Watchlist cards: 64x64 thumbnail on the left (spinner while pending, then a photo or a bag icon), 'Usually' and the price on the right, and a 44x40 trash icon below the price inside the card on all 6 cards. Tapping trash removes the item without opening edit; Undo restores it; tapping the card opens /add-item with the item's values. Main finding: the product-photo lookup is unreliable because Open Food Facts search often returns 503. Only 0-2 of 6 demo items got a photo per fresh demo user, and a failed lookup is saved permanently as 'no photo'. No deprecated Expo packages found (expo-av, expo-barcode-scanner, expo-background-fetch not in package.json).

critical.issue: Open Food Facts cgi/search.pl often returns HTTP 503 'Service Temporarily Unavailable' (rate limit; backend log has 133 'Image lookup failed ... Expecting value' lines). The code calls r.json() without checking the status, and the except branch saves image_url=None, image_checked=True, so a temporary outage becomes a permanent bag icon (the only retry is editing the item). Each new demo user also repeats the same 6 lookups, which makes the rate limiting worse. Seen: run 1 got 2/6 photos (Cheerios, Milk); a later demo session got 0/6, Cheerios included.

minor.issue: Duplicate stores are accepted and saved: {stores:['Aldi','Aldi']} returns 200 with stores ['Aldi','Aldi']. Also ['Kroger'] x7 passes max_length=7. The UI can't send duplicates, but the API should de-duplicate or reject them.
Flaky: one 502 during the parallel pytest run; passed on rerun (0.7 s, 200). Probably upstream or ingress under load.

integration_issues.issue: Most cards show the bag fallback instead of a photo because of the backend lookup issue above (OFF 503s saved as permanent 'no photo'). The UI itself (spinner, then image or bag) works.

issues: The 'On sale' pill plus the price column leaves little room for the name: 'Laundry Dete…' and 'Boneless Chicken Brea…' are cut off at 390 px. Consider moving the 'On sale' tag to the meta line or under the name.
Before scrolling, the FAB (60x60, bottom-right) covers the trash icon of the last visible card (Large Eggs at 390x844). The 104 px bottom padding fixes it after scrolling, so this is minor.

action_items: Make the photo lookup handle failures: check r.status_code (and content-type) before r.json(). On 5xx or 429 or a network error, leave image_checked=False (or store image_retry_at with backoff) instead of saving a permanent 'no photo'. Only set image_checked=True with image_url=None when OFF actually returned no match.

Cache photo lookups across users (e.g. a db.product_images collection keyed by barcode or a normalised 'brand name' string), and/or seed the 6 demo items with image_url or barcodes. This stops every new demo user making 6 rate-limited OFF search calls, and space the calls out (OFF search allows about 10 requests/min).
De-duplicate stores in OnboardingIn (e.g. a validator returning list(dict.fromkeys(stores))), or return 422 for duplicates.
Optional: move the 'On sale' pill so names aren't cut off; keep the FAB from covering the last card's trash icon.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:356/363: r.json() runs without a status check, so a 503 HTML page raises JSONDecodeError, which the except treats as 'no photo'.
server.py:381: the except branch saves a permanent negative result; this should only happen when no match was found.
server.py:152: max_length=len(STORES) is correct, but there is no uniqueness check.
Frontend refetchInterval 5 s while any item is unchecked (api.ts:66) is fine, and it stops once everything is checked.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_promobeaux_api.py (422 cases now [] and 8 stores; me check now allows 1..7 stores)

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows work; photo coverage poor because of the backend lookup issue

context_for_next_testing_agent: Demo login lands on the Deals tab. Tab testIDs: tab-deals, tab-watchlist, tab-savings, tab-profile. The store picker is /onboarding?edit=1 from profile-edit-stores-button. Open Food Facts search is rate limited (503s), so photo results vary between runs; check backend.err.log for 'Image lookup failed'. Run pytest with -n 0 for live-check tests to avoid flaky 502s.
rca_of_issue: Missing photos: OFF /cgi/search.pl returns 503 under rate limiting. lookup_product_image calls r.json() on the HTML 503 body, which raises JSONDecodeError. fill_images catches it and saves image_checked=True with image_url=None, so the app shows the bag icon permanently. Reproduce: create 2-3 demo users quickly, wait 20 s, and GET /api/watchlist: most items have image_checked=true and image_url=null, and the log shows 503s. Fix: status-aware handling with retry/backoff, plus a cross-user cache.
